note: Susiana and the lower Karun are Elamite; the Sumerian alluvium ends at the Tigris marshes.
Same line as Sumer's. Akkad raided Susa but the frontier of settlement is the Tigris.
Same line again: Old Babylon and Elam divide at Susiana, which is Elam's core.

The Amuq and the lower Orontes are never Egyptian. Thutmose III's furthest campaigns raided past Aleppo but held nothing north of the Orontes bend; Suppiluliuma I made north Syria Hittite outright, and the treaty after Kadesh (1259) fixed the frontier at Kadesh, a hundred and fifty kilometres south of the ground the two extents shared.
Tyre, Sidon and Byblos paid tribute but were never provinces; the Assyrian border runs inland of the coast road.
Same coastal strip, same reason: Nebuchadnezzar besieged Tyre for thirteen years without taking it.
Nabopolassar's revolt, 626: Babylonia and then the Levant leave Assyria, which keeps only the northern heartland to 609.
Ionia is a Persian satrapy from 546 and again from 387; the Aegean cities on the Asian shore are drawn Persian.
The Sicilian frontier is the Halycus. Selinus and Akragas east of it are Greek; Punic Sicily is the west.
European Thrace was lost to Persia in 479; from Philip's death it is unambiguously Macedonian.

The Ordos loop and the Hexi corridor go to Han in the campaigns of 127 and 121 BCE, and the wall is rebuilt along them; the Xiongnu frontier is the steppe beyond it. The Han side keeps the ground because the wall is a line somebody built and the steppe boundary is not.
The 303 treaty: Seleucus cedes Gandhara, Arachosia and Gedrosia to Chandragupta for five hundred elephants.
Ipsus 301 to Panium 200: Coele-Syria is Ptolemaic, and the Seleucid claim to it is a claim, not a border.
Panium, 200: Coele-Syria passes to Antiochus III and never returns.
Sistan and Aria are Kushan while the Kushans are a power; Parthia's east ends at the Herat corridor.
Ardashir and Shapur I take Bactria and Gandhara; what is left of the Kushans rules under Sasanian suzerainty.
Yarmuk 636 and the fall of Alexandria 642: Syria and Egypt are gone. Byzantium keeps Anatolia, the Balkans and the west.
The same conquest continued — Carthage 698 — so the African exarchate goes too.
The caliphate crosses the Red Sea in the extent polygon and never did on the ground: the Ethiopian highlands stay Aksumite, and Islam arrived there by treaty, not conquest.
As above.
As above.
The Taurus is the frontier and Cilicia is the Muslim thughur: Tarsus and Melitene are Abbasid, the passes are Byzantine.
The Fatimid conquest of Egypt, 969; Ifriqiya had gone in 909.

Antioch and the lower Orontes are Byzantine from Nikephoros Phokas' reconquest in 969 and Frankish after 1098; the Fatimids never held the Amuq. Their reach up the Syrian coast tops out at Tripoli, and after 1070 not even that.
Before Manzikert's consequences settle, Anatolia is Byzantine and the Seljuks are an Iranian and Mesopotamian power.
And after: the interior plateau is the Sultanate of Rum, the coasts and the Balkans stay Byzantine.
The Huai is the frontier. Everything north of it was lost with the Jin in 1234.
After Ain Jalut the Euphrates is the line; Aleppo and northern Syria are Mamluk.
By 1450 Byzantium is the city, its Thracian hinterland gone; the Morea is the only other piece.
The 1297 Alcanices border. Spain yields it until the union of crowns.
…and again from the Restoration War: the union of 1580-1640 is the one period when Castile really does hold Lisbon, and the keyframe at 1640 is where it ends.
The Zuhab line, 1639, which is where the Ottoman-Persian frontier ends up and mostly sat: Baghdad and Iraq are Ottoman.
Deulino, 1618: Smolensk and Chernihiv are Polish-Lithuanian until the war of 1654.
Nerchinsk, 1689: the Amur basin is Qing and Russia's line runs along the Stanovoy range.
Aigun 1858 and Peking 1860 reverse it: Outer Manchuria and the Ussuri become Russian.
Tonkin was a tributary, never a province, and is French from 1885.

The Yalu is the frontier. Ming proclaimed a Tieling commandery on the Korean side of the river in 1388 and withdrew it within five years; from 1393 the Liaodong border ends at the Yalu and the eastern bank — Uiju up to the Paektu watershed — is Joseon's. Joseon sent tribute missions and was never a Ming province.

The same two rivers, the Yalu and the Tumen, surveyed onto the ground by Mukedeng in 1712 and marked with a stele on the watershed between their sources. The Qing bank is a closed frontier zone behind the willow palisade; the Korean bank is Joseon's. Tributary status is not a border, which is why the Qing extent's straight line across the northern peninsula yields to the rivers.

The same rivers after 1897. Shimonoseki (1895) ended the Qing claim to suzerainty outright — article 1 recognises Korea as fully independent — so what the two extents still share here is only the Qing polygon's straight-line drawing of the lower Yalu.
Shimonoseki: Taiwan is ceded and Korea leaves the Qing orbit; Japan annexes it in 1910.
The Tumen: the Russo-Korean border of 1860 is not moved by the annexation of Korea.
Paris 1783 and the Convention of 1818: the Great Lakes line and then the 49th parallel.
The Berlin conference: German East Africa, South West Africa, Kamerun and Togo are German until 1918, British mandates after.

The Treaty of Frankfurt, 1871: Alsace and the Moselle are annexed to the Reich and stay German until 1918, which is the whole of Germany's existence in this corpus. France keeps its 1840 keyframe otherwise.
The 1815 Congress Poland border: Suwalki and the Vistula bend are Russian.
The Pyrenean crest, fixed by the Treaty of the Pyrenees in 1659 with Roussillon and Cerdagne French.
New France is French until the Treaty of Paris: the Saint Lawrence, the Great Lakes and the Ohio country are not British before 1763.
The Niger and Lake Chad conventions of 1890-1906: northern Nigeria is British, the Sahel around it French.
The occupation of Egypt, 1882, and the Taba line of 1906: Sinai is administered from Cairo.

Jassy 1792 put the frontier on the Dniester and Bucharest 1812 moved it to the Prut: the Budjak between them is Russian for the rest of the Ottoman span. Dated from 1812 so it cannot reach back past the 1800 keyframe's neighbours.
The Sino-Soviet border of 1949 is the one the Qing lost in 1860; it does not move.
Tonkin again: French Indochina until 1954.
